the three-state model for Na channel blocker interaction is consistent with the noise data.

the three-state kinetic scheme of blocker interactions with Na channels in frog skin epithelial cells is consistent with a model of a channel that has a low open probability and a high rate of opening and closing, a model that is consistent with the notion of the channel being in a highly dynamic state in which it is constantly opening and closing in a random fashion.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the Na channel is predominantly in the open state in the absence of blockers, that blockers interact primarily with the open state and that the blocker interaction rate is faster than channel opening.
the kinetic model of the apical Na channel of frog skin is a three-state model where blocker interacts predominantly with the open state.
the kinetic scheme for blocker interaction with the apical Na channel is best described as a three-state model with blocker interacting only with the open state.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the Na channels of frog epithelial tissues are not in a steady state with respect to blocker-induced autoregulation.
Na channels of frog apical membranes can be in a state where blocker interaction is minimal, i.e., a state where the channels are not open.
the Na channel of frog skin is not a "simple" two-state channel.
